whyPeopleFallInLove: People arrive for wildlife safaris in Periyar National Park. They stay for the intoxicating aroma of fresh spices wafting through the local markets. They return because Thekkady offers a sensory feast that combines wild adventures with the richness of Kerala's culinary heritage, like no other place in India.
honestTruth: Most guides will tell you about the safaris, but they miss that the real magic lies in the interactions with local spice plantations, where you can learn to cook traditional dishes with ingredients harvested just moments before.
localTruths: Most visitors think they should spend all day in the national park. Locals think the real experience includes early morning visits to spice farms for hands-on cooking lessons.
Most visitors flock to the typical tourist restaurants. The best version of Thekkady is found in family-run eateries where the food tells stories of generations.
Most visitors spend too much time at the entrance of Periyar National Park. The real Thekkady starts at the vibrant spice market, where you can taste local delicacies.
